bio:
Data engineer at Recruit Co., Ltd., working on data management and data engineering. On Kaggle I'll take on anything — tabular, CV, optimization, agents. 
Trust your CV.
Measure, don't guess.

badge.name: 1 Year on Kaggle
badge.description: Active on Kaggle for more than 1 year.

badge.name: 2 Years on Kaggle
badge.description: Active on Kaggle for more than 2 years.

badge.name: 5 Years on Kaggle
badge.description: Active on Kaggle for more than 5 years.

badge.name: Competitor
badge.description: Made a submission to a Kaggle competition that is eligible for points or medals. These competitions are full-scale machine learning challenges which pose difficult real world prediction problems.

badge.name: Getting Started Competitor
badge.description: Made a submission to a Getting Started competition. Getting Started competitions are the easiest, most approachable competitions on Kaggle used as introductions to the field of machine learning.

badge.name: Research Competitor
badge.description: Made a submission to a Research competition. Research competitions feature problems which are more experimental, may not have a clean or easy solution, and which are integral to a specific domain.

badge.name: Community Competitor
badge.description: Made a submission to a Community competition. These competitions are created by other Kagglers including educators, researchers, companies, meetup groups, or hackathon hosts.

badge.name: Simulation Competitor
badge.description: Made a submission to a Simulation competition. These competitions challenge participants to create intelligent agents which compete in unique game environments.

badge.name: Santa Competitor
badge.description: Made a submission to a Santa competition. Santa competitions are Kaggle's annual tradition of hosting a holiday competition focussed on optimization problems.

badge.name: Code Submitter
badge.description: Made a submission to a code competition. These competitions require the submission of a reproducible bundle of code rather than a simple file of predictions.

badge.name: Submission Streak
badge.description: Submitted to a competition for 7 days in a row.

badge.name: Python Coder
badge.description: Created a python notebook. Python is one of the most popular general purpose programming languages and has gained widespread use in the machine learning community.

badge.name: Code Uploader
badge.description: Uploaded a notebook. With the import feature you can upload notebook files to Kaggle. This allows you to work on your local machine and upload your work when you are ready to share or submit it.

badge.name: API Notebook Creator
badge.description: Imported a notebook using the Kaggle API. Use the Kaggle API for convenience or as part of an automated workflow.

badge.name: Github Coder
badge.description: Imported a notebook from Github or linked a notebook to Github. You can import or sync notebooks from Github. When synced each version you save on Kaggle can be committed back to your Github repo.

badge.name: Colab Coder
badge.description: Imported a notebook from Colab or opened a notebook in Colab. You can easily import notebooks from Colab (to share or submit on Kaggle). Likewise you can open any Kaggle notebook in Colab to edit.

badge.name: Code Tagger
badge.description: Added tags to a notebook. Tagging a notebook makes it more discoverable across Kaggle.

badge.name: Code Forker
badge.description: Copied a notebook and made changes to it. Copying a notebook (also known as 'forking' a notebook) is a great way to save time, allowing you to quickly build on top of publicly shared work.

badge.name: Notebook Modeler
badge.description: Used a model in a notebook. Pretrained models from the Kaggle Model Hub are powerful tools for taking your work to the next level.

badge.name: Dataset Creator
badge.description: Created a dataset. It’s easy to create a dataset on Kaggle and doing so is a great way to start a data science portfolio, share reproducible research, or work with collaborators on a project.

badge.name: Dataset Pipeline Creator
badge.description: Created a dataset from notebook output. Creating a dataset from a notebook’s output files will let you create reproducible data pipelines. This can also be used to automatically update datasets.

badge.name: API Dataset Creator
badge.description: Created a dataset using the Kaggle API. Use the Kaggle API for convenience or as part of an automated workflow.

badge.name: Dataset Tagger
badge.description: Added tags to a dataset. Tagging a dataset makes it more discoverable across Kaggle.

badge.name: Model Creator
badge.description: Created a model. Kaggle Models is a repository of pre-trained models that are deeply integrated with Kaggle's platform, making them easy to use in Kaggle Competitions and Notebooks.

badge.name: Competition Modeler
badge.description: Used a model in a competition notebook. Pretrained models are powerful tools for taking your competition submissions to the next level.

badge.name: Kaggle Community Member
badge.description: Joined the Kaggle Community by creating an account. The first step in a great adventure!

badge.name: Bookmarker
badge.description: Bookmarked something on Kaggle. Most things on Kaggle can be bookmarked. You can view your bookmarks in the sidebar or the 'Your Work' section to quickly get back to them.

badge.name: Vampire
badge.description: Turned on the Kaggle dark theme. You can make this change under settings. Dark mode is a popular alternative color scheme for the site which many people find easier on the eyes.

badge.name: 7 Day Login Streak
badge.description: Logged in to Kaggle 7 days in a row.

badge.name: 30 Day Login Streak
badge.description: Logged in to Kaggle 30 days in a row.
